evidence.claim: The Government of Pakistan and the UN jointly launched the 2022 Floods Response Plan after floods and landslides affected more than 33 million people and killed more than 1,100, with the plan targeting 5.2 million people and including protection, health, water, women's health, and education support.
evidence.title: Media Update: United Nations Pakistan, 30 August 2022
evidence.excerpt: The Government of Pakistan and the UN jointly launched the 2022 Floods Response Plan after floods and landslides affected more than 33 million people and killed more than 1,100, with the plan targeting 5.2 million people and including protection, health, water, women's health, and education support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN release with government participation, concrete casualty figures, and plan scope.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Sharif-era response, though the disaster itself was climate-driven and largely inherited as an external shock.
contrary_evidence: The plan describes response and relief, not proof of full effectiveness or long-term recovery.

evidence.claim: UNFPA said 6.4 million people needed humanitarian assistance, nearly 650,000 pregnant women required maternal services, damaged health facilities and roads limited access to care, and women and girls faced heightened gender-based violence risk.
evidence.title: Women and girls bearing the brunt of the Pakistan Monsoon floods
evidence.excerpt: UNFPA said 6.4 million people needed humanitarian assistance, nearly 650,000 pregnant women required maternal services, damaged health facilities and roads limited access to care, and women and girls faced heightened gender-based violence risk.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official UN agency response with precise needs estimates and vulnerable-group impacts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Sharif-era crisis management and vulnerable-group protection, with the underlying disaster mostly inherited from climate conditions.
contrary_evidence: This is a humanitarian snapshot, not a full audit of the government's performance.

evidence.claim: The PDNA estimated total flood damages above USD 14.9 billion, losses around USD 15.2 billion, and reconstruction needs of at least USD 16.3 billion for resilient recovery.
evidence.title: Pakistan Floods 2022: Post-Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA)
evidence.excerpt: The PDNA estimated total flood damages above USD 14.9 billion, losses around USD 15.2 billion, and reconstruction needs of at least USD 16.3 billion for resilient recovery.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Jointly prepared disaster assessment with clear damage and recovery estimates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Contextual end-state measure of a disaster-driven year, not a discrete Sharif decision.
contrary_evidence: A damage estimate is not the same as a ruler-performance finding, but it is important for the inherited safety baseline.

evidence.claim: On the prime minister's directions, the finance minister pursued targeted subsidy proposals to provide immediate relief to lower-income households under a PM relief package.
evidence.title: Federal Minister for Finance and Revenue presided over a meeting on PM Relief Package through USC
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: On the prime minister's directions, the finance minister pursued targeted subsidy proposals to provide immediate relief to lower-income households under a PM relief package.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government release with direct policy description and named participants.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and while Sharif's cabinet was defining its economic response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Sharif's directions, though implementation ran through the finance and social safety ministries.
contrary_evidence: The release is a policy announcement, not proof of successful delivery at scale.

evidence.claim: The World Bank projected only 2 percent growth in FY2023 and said the slowdown reflected flood damage, tight monetary policy, high inflation, and a weaker global environment, with poverty likely to worsen absent decisive relief.
evidence.title: Pakistan's Economy Slows Down While Inflation Rises Amid Catastrophic Floods
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank projected only 2 percent growth in FY2023 and said the slowdown reflected flood damage, tight monetary policy, high inflation, and a weaker global environment, with poverty likely to worsen absent decisive relief.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank assessment with explicit macro and poverty projections.
evidence.period_fit: Late 2022 and directly relevant to end-of-year economic trajectory under Sharif.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly external shocks and inherited macro weakness, but the government's relief and stabilization response still matters for attribution.
contrary_evidence: This source attributes a large part of the deterioration to floods and external conditions rather than solely to Sharif's choices.

evidence.claim: UNDP said the 2022 floods were Pakistan's worst disaster in decades, affecting 33 million people, pushing about 8 million into poverty, and destroying about 2 million houses, while recovery was framed around gender equality and resilience.
evidence.title: Flood Recovery Programme
evidence.excerpt: UNDP said the 2022 floods were Pakistan's worst disaster in decades, affecting 33 million people, pushing about 8 million into poverty, and destroying about 2 million houses, while recovery was framed around gender equality and resilience.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNDP programme page summarizing humanitarian and recovery impacts with clear household-distribution consequences.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to household-level welfare at the end of Sharif's first year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is mostly disaster context, not a direct ruler-policy claim, but it sets the welfare baseline for evaluating response and distribution.
contrary_evidence: The effects stem from floods, not from an economic policy decision by Sharif.

evidence.claim: The poverty-alleviation ministry said the present government was using data, technology, financial inclusion, women’s empowerment, human-capital formation, and reduced barriers to health and education to build a welfare state.
evidence.title: SCO International Forum for Poverty Alleviation is a great effort, Shazia Marri
evidence.excerpt: The poverty-alleviation ministry said the present government was using data, technology, financial inclusion, women’s empowerment, human-capital formation, and reduced barriers to health and education to build a welfare state.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct government statement by the responsible minister in 2022; rhetoric is explicit, though implementation still needs corroboration.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sharif-led federal government through its poverty-alleviation ministry; it reflects stated policy intent more than measurable delivery.
contrary_evidence: This is mainly an intent statement and does not by itself prove implementation or outcomes.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved $258 million for Pakistan’s National Health Support Program to strengthen primary health care and accelerate universal health coverage, with emphasis on communities lagging behind and on access for children and women during pregnancy and childbirth.
evidence.title: World Bank Supports Primary Healthcare and Universal Coverage to Strengthen Human Capital in Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved $258 million for Pakistan’s National Health Support Program to strengthen primary health care and accelerate universal health coverage, with emphasis on communities lagging behind and on access for children and women during pregnancy and childbirth.
evidence.source_locator: press release lead and program summary
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release with concrete financing and program design details.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and under the Sharif government.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sharif-led government’s health policy environment, but financed and implemented with provincial and donor participation.
contrary_evidence: World Bank financing is not the same as Sharif personally designing or executing the program.

evidence.claim: UNICEF and the Government of Pakistan set a strategy to protect and promote diets, practices, and services supporting women’s health and well-being, with evidence-based and equity-based nutrition programmes at scale for preconception, pregnancy, and postpartum periods.
evidence.title: Pakistan Maternal Nutrition Strategy 2022-27
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF and the Government of Pakistan set a strategy to protect and promote diets, practices, and services supporting women’s health and well-being, with evidence-based and equity-based nutrition programmes at scale for preconception, pregnancy, and postpartum periods.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Joint UNICEF-government strategy document with clear program goals and target groups.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sharif-era federal government working with UNICEF; implementation was shared with health systems and provinces.
contrary_evidence: This is a strategy document rather than proof of nationwide delivery in 2022.

evidence.claim: WHO said Pakistan had approved a limited national Essential Package of Health Services for immediate district-level implementation and had localized the package into provincial plans and budgets in all provinces except Punjab by May 2022.
evidence.title: Towards sustainable financing for PHC and UHC: The piloting of Essential Package of Health Services in Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: WHO said Pakistan had approved a limited national Essential Package of Health Services for immediate district-level implementation and had localized the package into provincial plans and budgets in all provinces except Punjab by May 2022.
evidence.source_locator: overview and 'Moving planning to results' sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: WHO feature story describing a concrete health-policy pilot and the status of localization in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Pakistan health system under the Sharif government; WHO and donors were co-implementers, so attribution is shared.
contrary_evidence: The story describes piloting and partial localization, not full national implementation.

evidence.claim: The finance minister said the Kamyab Pakistan Program was consistent with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s vision to improve living standards and would provide interest-free loans to poorer segments through a bottom-up approach.
evidence.title: PR No.53
evidence.excerpt: The finance minister said the Kamyab Pakistan Program was consistent with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s vision to improve living standards and would provide interest-free loans to poorer segments through a bottom-up approach.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct government press release naming the program, purpose, and beneficiary design.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and Sharif’s first months in office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sharif-led federal government through the finance ministry; this is an intent-and-design source more than a delivery audit.
contrary_evidence: The release does not establish whether the program materially improved incomes in 2022.

evidence.claim: The prime minister directed that every flood-affected family receive Rs. 50,000 within three days, with BISP cash relief delivered under NDMA supervision and via electronic transfer so deserving people would get relief.
evidence.title: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed to ensure the provision of Rs. 50,000 relief to each flood affected family through a transparent process within the three days
evidence.excerpt: The prime minister directed that every flood-affected family receive Rs. 50,000 within three days, with BISP cash relief delivered under NDMA supervision and via electronic transfer so deserving people would get relief.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PM instruction recorded in the official press release with concrete amount, mechanism, and delivery timeline.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Shehbaz Sharif as prime minister; operational delivery still depended on BISP, NDMA, and provincial machinery.
contrary_evidence: This was emergency relief, not a durable reform of ordinary welfare provision.

evidence.claim: BISP said the federal government increased the flood-relief cash package from Rs. 28 billion to Rs. 70 billion and was distributing Rs. 25,000 per family transparently, including in Gilgit-Baltistan.
evidence.title: Federal Government has increased the amount of flood relief package to Rupees 70 billion
evidence.excerpt: BISP said the federal government increased the flood-relief cash package from Rs. 28 billion to Rs. 70 billion and was distributing Rs. 25,000 per family transparently, including in Gilgit-Baltistan.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government social-protection agency reporting specific package size, transfer amount, and coverage expansion.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and the flood response window.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sharif-led federal government, though BISP executed the disbursements and provincial/local conditions shaped access.
contrary_evidence: Again, this is crisis relief rather than evidence of a strengthened ordinary welfare system.

evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif launched the 4RF for Pakistan Floods 2022, a short-, medium-, and long-term climate-resilient recovery and reconstruction framework based on the PDNA and presented as an inclusive whole-of-Pakistan approach.
evidence.title: PR No. 177 PRIME MINISTER OF PAKISTAN MUHAMMAD SHEHBAZ SHARIF LAUNCHES THE RESILIENT, RECOVERY, REHABILITATION AND RECONSTRUCTION FRAMEWORK (4RF) FOR PAKISTAN FLOODS
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif launched the 4RF for Pakistan Floods 2022, a short-, medium-, and long-term climate-resilient recovery and reconstruction framework based on the PDNA and presented as an inclusive whole-of-Pakistan approach.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct PM launch notice with concrete policy architecture and timing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sharif, though the framework itself was prepared with ministries, provinces, and development partners.
contrary_evidence: A framework is not the same as measured reconstruction completion.

evidence.claim: WFP said it was expanding food assistance, malnutrition prevention, and livelihoods support for flood-affected families while the Government of Pakistan, through NDMA, was leading the response and coordinating relief.
evidence.title: WFP steps up humanitarian support to government relief efforts as Pakistan reels from devastating floods
evidence.excerpt: WFP said it was expanding food assistance, malnutrition prevention, and livelihoods support for flood-affected families while the Government of Pakistan, through NDMA, was leading the response and coordinating relief.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary WFP operational report with explicit role assignment and concrete assistance categories.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sharif government as the leading national authority, but the response was multiactor and heavily dependent on humanitarian partners.
contrary_evidence: The same source underscores that the disaster had overwhelmed domestic capacity and required external support.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said more than 2 million children remained out of school after floods damaged or destroyed nearly 27,000 schools and that it had established more than 500 temporary learning centres and supported teachers and children with supplies.
evidence.title: Schools for more than 2 million children in Pakistan remain inaccessible due to devastating floods
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said more than 2 million children remained out of school after floods damaged or destroyed nearly 27,000 schools and that it had established more than 500 temporary learning centres and supported teachers and children with supplies.
evidence.source_locator: press release body and notes for editors
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF release with specific counts and response measures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is mostly crisis-context and partner response, not a PM-specific claim, but it defines the child-welfare stakes of the Sharif period.
contrary_evidence: The source highlights continuing educational deprivation rather than a clean welfare improvement.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved five projects for flood-affected Sindh, including social protection delivery, conditional cash transfers for 1.3 million mothers and children, and health services for women, girls, and children in flood-affected settlements.
evidence.title: Pakistan: World Bank Approves $1.692 Billion for 5 Projects to Support the People of Sindh in the Flood-Affected Areas
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved five projects for flood-affected Sindh, including social protection delivery, conditional cash transfers for 1.3 million mothers and children, and health services for women, girls, and children in flood-affected settlements.
evidence.source_locator: press release body, especially project descriptions
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary financing announcement with specific beneficiary groups and delivery mechanisms.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and relevant to the end-of-year welfare trajectory.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sharif government’s recovery agenda, though financed and structured jointly with the World Bank and implemented at provincial level.
contrary_evidence: Province-specific recovery financing does not by itself show nationwide welfare improvement by year-end.

unresolved_gaps: No independent 2022 evidence of a Sharif-chaired NCA session or any doctrine, custody, or command-and-control reform.
No direct evidence of Sharif's handling of dual-use, proliferation, cyber, biosecurity, or AI-risk policy in 2022.
The April 2022 Afghanistan strike allegation remains unresolved by an independent finding or clear attribution chain.
No formal ceasefire or settlement output with India or Afghanistan beyond public diplomacy and border-management statements.
Primary court orders or audit findings on the Ramzan Sugar Mills and Ashiana matters are still needed to separate allegations from a durable personal-nexus finding.
The appointment/favoritism question still lacks stronger evidence about whether key personnel choices reflected merit or protection of insiders.

run_provenance.source_mix_note: Rich source metadata and chapter-specific reviewer exclusions were preserved during deterministic conversion.
